result:
This goes through the new-project path. Nothing is built yet, and `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md` is a research brief, not a spec with numbered requirements. So I treat the brief as your own statement of what you want, and the three research files as background for facts and costs only. Everything below comes from the brief. Before I write any roadmap text, I need your ranking.

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome: what you get | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | Size of total-nonfarm revisions over time for each of the four revisions (1st→2nd, 2nd→3rd, 3rd→benchmark, post-benchmark/wedge-back), with 2003 and 2020–22 marked | Small data: a few MB (one series × several hundred monthly vintages × about 1,000 months). Count of ALFRED vintages and earliest vintage date unconfirmed. FRED's published API limit is 120 requests/min (to confirm). |
| O2 | The same history by NAICS supersector | ALFRED's supersector vintage coverage is unknown. If gaps need hand-collection from archived releases, your time is the main cost. Unknown until checked. |
| O3 | News vs. noise share of each of the four revisions, from a latent "true employment" path observed through each vintage | Fit time unknown: only running it can tell. |
| O4 | Size of the benchmark error and how wedge-back spreads it over the intervening months, with the benchmark as a precise, irregular observation | Only about 40 annual benchmarks, so little information. Fit time is measured by running it. |
| O5 | Share of seasonally adjusted (SA) revisions due to seasonal-factor revision vs. sample revision, from joint not-seasonally-adjusted (NSA) and SA vintages | Depends on NSA vintage availability. A PAYNSA vintage history in ALFRED is unconfirmed. |
| O6 | Effect of collection interval (days from the 12th to release) and first-closing rate on the size of the one- and two-month revisions | About 500 release dates turned into collection days (arithmetic from release calendars). The start year of published collection-rate history is to confirm. |
| O7 | Association of BLS funding, staffing and sample size with revision size, reported with explicit limits on what is identified; party as a description only | Hand-built annual covariates: about 40 values each from budget justifications, FedScope and benchmark articles. Days of your time. |
| O8 | Driver effects by supersector, partially pooled | Scales O6 and O7 by 11 or more supersectors. Fit time is measured by running it. |

Qualities to place when the roadmap is written: point-in-time awareness, traceability, manifests, full validation suites.

## Tracks

- **A — Revision history (O1, O2).** Proposed as a known progression: total nonfarm, then supersectors. Please confirm you can name its steps.
- **B — Measurement model (O3, O4).** Research. Split from A because the descriptive history stands without a latent model.
- **C — Seasonal vs. sample (O5).** Research. Split because the decomposition comes from joint NSA/SA vintage accounting and stands without the news/noise model.
- **D — Collection interval (O6, O8).** Research. Split from E because the calendar-driven effect within a year stands without the slow capacity covariates, and joined, it would wait on hand-building those covariates.
- **E — Operational capacity (O7).** Research. It is weakly identified and depends on hand-built inputs.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 with uv. Whether JAX, NumPyro and Dynamax support 3.14 is unconfirmed and worth a cheap check.
- NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax for marginalizing the linear-Gaussian state, Blackjax only if needed, ArviZ, Polars.
- Bayesian estimation, with covariates entering the scale, not only the mean.
- Units: thousands of jobs.
- Party of the appropriators: descriptive grouping only.

**Proposed roadmap name:** `ces-revisions`, giving `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`.

## Request

Please rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves. Also confirm or change the tracks, their kinds (especially A as a known progression) and the name.

If you want firmer costs for O1, O2 and O5 first, I can run one small probe: list the ALFRED vintages for PAYEMS, PAYNSA and one supersector series. It needs a FRED API key from you and sends nothing about you or the project. Say yes only if you want it.
